subject: Business Models
title: Embedded Finance
description: A quick win: understand Embedded Finance.

hook.text: Shopify lends money to its merchants. Uber offers instant driver payouts. Non-banks are becoming banks.

buildup.text: Embedded finance integrates banking services (lending, payments, insurance) into non-financial products.

discovery.text: Companies already have the customer data and trust. Adding financial services captures revenue banks used to own.

twist.text: Embedded finance could be worth $7 trillion by 2030. Every company with customer data becomes a potential bank.

climax.text: Finance is becoming invisible—embedded into the products you already use, not applications you visit separately.

punchline.text: Shopify lends, Uber pays out, Apple offers savings. Every company is a bank now.

quiz.question: What is embedded finance?
options: Integrating financial services into non-financial products

details.summary: Embedded finance integrates banking, lending, insurance, and payment services directly into non-financial platforms and apps. Instead of visiting a bank, customers access financial products seamlessly within the software they already use for shopping, accounting, or ride-sharing.
details.whyItMatters: Embedded finance represents a multi-trillion dollar opportunity. It lets any company become a fintech by offering branded financial products, generating new revenue while improving customer experience and retention.
takeaways: Financial services are embedded directly into non-financial platforms
APIs from banking-as-a-service providers enable rapid integration
Non-financial companies earn interchange, interest, and insurance fees

faq.question: What are examples of embedded finance in everyday products?
faq.answer: Buy-now-pay-later at e-commerce checkout, insurance offered during ride-hailing booking, instant lending within accounting software, branded debit cards from gig platforms, and savings accounts inside payroll apps are all embedded finance in action.

faq.question: How do non-financial companies profit from embedded finance?
faq.answer: They earn interchange fees on card transactions, interest margins on lending, insurance commissions, and payment processing fees. They also benefit from increased customer retention and higher spending within their ecosystem.
